title: Cost of sequencing a human genome, 2001–2022
description: Bar chart on a logarithmic scale of the cost of sequencing a human-sized genome at the sequencing centers funded by the US National Human Genome Research Institute. September 2001: $95.3 million. October 2003: $40.2 million. October 2005: $13.8 million. October 2007: $7.1 million. October 2009: $70,333. October 2011: $7,743. October 2013: $5,096. October 2015: $1,245. November 2017: $1,844. November 2019: $695. November 2021: $552. May 2022: $525. The fall steepens after January 2008, when the centers changed to second-generation sequencing machines. Data: NHGRI, DNA Sequencing Costs: Data.
heading: COST PER HUMAN GENOME (NHGRI) · LOG SCALE
